verses.textEnNkjv: They also took away the pots, the shovels, the trimmers, the bowls, the spoons, and all the bronze utensils with which the priests ministered.
verses.textEnNlt: They also took all the ash buckets, shovels, lamp snuffers, basins, dishes, and all the other bronze articles used for making sacrifices at the Temple.
verses.textEnNasb: They also took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the basins, the pans, and all the bronze vessels which were used in temple service.
verses.textEn: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.

verses.textZh: 此外，碗盆、火鼎、碗、锅、灯台、碟子和奠酒的爵，无论是金的或是银的，护卫长都拿去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 此外，碗盆、火鼎、碗、锅、灯台、碟子和奠酒的爵，无论是金的或是银的，护卫长都拿去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 杯、火鼎、碗、盆、灯台、调羹、爵，无论金的银的，护卫长也都带去了。
verses.textEnNiv: The commander of the imperial guard took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes and bowls used for drink offerings—all that were made of pure gold or silver.
verses.textEnEsv: also the small bowls and the fire pans and the basins and the pots and the lampstands and the dishes for incense and the bowls for drink offerings. What was of gold the captain of the guard took away as gold, and what was of silver, as silver.
verses.textEnNkjv: The basins, the firepans, the bowls, the pots, the lampstands, the spoons, and the cups, whatever was solid gold and whatever was solid silver, the captain of the guard took away.
verses.textEnNlt: The captain of the guard also took the small bowls, incense burners, basins, pots, lampstands, ladles, bowls used for liquid offerings, and all the other articles made of pure gold or silver.
verses.textEnNasb: The captain of the guard also took the bowls, the firepans, the basins, the pots, the lampstands, the pans, and the drink offering bowls, whatever was fine gold, and whatever was fine silver.
verses.textEn: The commander of the imperial guard took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes and bowls used for drink offerings—all that were made of pure gold or silver.

verses.textZh: 所罗门王为耶和华的殿所做的两根铜柱、一个铜海、铜海下面的十二头铜牛，和十个铜座，这一切器皿的铜，重得无法可称。
verses.textZhCnvs: 所罗门王为耶和华的殿所做的两根铜柱、一个铜海、铜海下面的十二头铜牛，和十个铜座，这一切器皿的铜，重得无法可称。
verses.textZhCuv: 所罗门为耶和华殿所造的两根铜柱、一个铜海，并座下的十二只铜牛，这一切的铜多得无法可称。
verses.textEnNiv: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands, which King Solomon had made for the temple of the Lord , was more than could be weighed.
verses.textEnEsv: As for the two pillars, the one sea, the twelve bronze bulls that were under the sea, and the stands, which Solomon the king had made for the house of the Lord , the bronze of all these things was beyond weight.
verses.textEnNkjv: The two pillars, one Sea, the twelve bronze bulls which were under it, and the carts, which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord— the bronze of all these articles was beyond measure.
verses.textEnNlt: The weight of the bronze from the two pillars, the Sea with the twelve bronze oxen beneath it, and the water carts was too great to be measured. These things had been made for the Lord ’s Temple in the days of King Solomon.
verses.textEnNasb: The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the sea, and the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord—the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weight.
verses.textEn: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands, which King Solomon had made for the temple of the Lord , was more than could be weighed.

verses.textZh: 至于那些柱子，每根高八公尺，圆周是五公尺三公分，柱子是空心的。铜的厚度有七十五公厘。
verses.textZhCnvs: 至于那些柱子，每根高八公尺，圆周是五公尺三公分，柱子是空心的。铜的厚度有七十五公厘。
verses.textZhCuv: 这一根柱子高十八肘，厚四指，是空的，围十二肘。
verses.textEnNiv: Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference ; each was four fingers thick, and hollow.
verses.textEnEsv: As for the pillars, the height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, its circumference was twelve cubits, and its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now concerning the pillars: the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, a measuring line of twelve cubits could measure its circumference, and its thickness was four fingers; itwas hollow.
verses.textEnNlt: Each of the pillars was 27 feet tall and 18 feet in circumference. They were hollow, with walls 3 inches thick.
verses.textEnNasb: As for the pillars, the height of each pillar was eighteen cubits, and it was twelve cubits in circumference and four fingers in thickness, and hollow.
verses.textEn: Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference ; each was four fingers thick, and hollow.

verses.textZh: 柱上有铜柱头，柱头高两公尺三十公分，柱头四周有网子和石榴都是铜的；另一根柱子同样也有石榴。
verses.textZhCnvs: 柱上有铜柱头，柱头高两公尺三十公分，柱头四周有网子和石榴都是铜的；另一根柱子同样也有石榴。
verses.textZhCuv: 柱上有铜顶，高五肘；铜顶的周围有网子和石榴，都是铜的。那一根柱子照此一样，也有石榴。
verses.textEnNiv: The bronze capital on top of one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.
verses.textEnEsv: On it was a capital of bronze. The height of the one capital was five cubits. A network and pomegranates, all of bronze, were around the capital. And the second pillar had the same, with pomegranates.
verses.textEnNkjv: A capital of bronze was on it; and the height of one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar, with pomegranates was the same.
verses.textEnNlt: The bronze capital on top of each pillar was 7-1/2 feet high and was decorated with a network of bronze pomegranates all the way around.
verses.textEnNasb: Also, a capital of bronze was on top of it; and the height of each capital was five cubits, with latticework and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of bronze. And the second pillar was like these, including pomegranates.
verses.textEn: The bronze capital on top of one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.

verses.textZh: 每个网子周围共有一百个石榴，明显可见的有九十六个。
verses.textZhCnvs: 每个网子周围共有一百个石榴，明显可见的有九十六个。
verses.textZhCuv: 柱子四面有九十六个石榴，在网子周围，共有一百石榴。
verses.textEnNiv: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; the total number of pomegranates above the surrounding network was a hundred.
verses.textEnEsv: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates were a hundred upon the network all around.
verses.textEnNkjv: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates, all around on the network, were one hundred.
verses.textEnNlt: There were 96 pomegranates on the sides, and a total of 100 pomegranates on the network around the top.
verses.textEnNasb: There were ninety-six exposed pomegranates; all the pomegranates numbered a hundred on the latticework all around.
verses.textEn: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; the total number of pomegranates above the surrounding network was a hundred.

verses.textZh: 护卫长拿住祭司长西莱雅、副祭司长西番亚和三个守门的；
verses.textZhCnvs: 护卫长拿住祭司长西莱雅、副祭司长西番亚和三个守门的；
verses.textZhCuv: 护卫长拿住大祭司西莱雅、副祭司西番亚，和三个把门的，
verses.textEnNiv: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.
verses.textEnEsv: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold;
verses.textEnNkjv: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.
verses.textEnNlt: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took with him as prisoners Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the priest of the second rank, and the three chief gatekeepers.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest, with the three officers of the temple.
verses.textEn: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.

verses.textZh: 又从城里拿住一个管理军兵的官长，并且在城里搜获常见王面的七个人，和一个负责召募当地人民的军长书记，又在城中搜获六十个当地的人民。
verses.textZhCnvs: 又从城里拿住一个管理军兵的官长，并且在城里搜获常见王面的七个人，和一个负责召募当地人民的军长书记，又在城中搜获六十个当地的人民。
verses.textZhCuv: 又从城中拿住一个管理兵丁的官 ，并在城里所遇常见王面的七个人和检点国民军长的书记，以及城里所遇见的国民六十个人。
verses.textEnNiv: Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men, and seven royal advisers. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land, sixty of whom were found in the city.
verses.textEnEsv: and from the city he took an officer who had been in command of the men of war, and seven men of the king’s council, who were found in the city; and the secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, who were found in the midst of the city.
verses.textEnNkjv: He also took out of the city an officer who had charge of the men of war, seven men of the king’s close associates who were found in the city, the principal scribe of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
verses.textEnNlt: And from among the people still hiding in the city, he took an officer who had been in charge of the Judean army; seven of the king’s personal advisers; the army commander’s chief secretary, who was in charge of recruitment; and sixty other citizens.
verses.textEnNasb: He also took from the city one official who was overseer of the warriors, seven of the king’s advisers who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found inside the city.
verses.textEn: Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men, and seven royal advisers. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land, sixty of whom were found in the city.

verses.textZh: 护卫长尼布撒拉旦把他们拿住，带到利比拉巴比伦王那里。
verses.textZhCnvs: 护卫长尼布撒拉旦把他们拿住，带到利比拉巴比伦王那里。
verses.textZhCuv: 护卫长尼布撒拉旦将这些人带到利比拉的巴比伦王那里。
verses.textEnNiv: Nebuzaradan the commander took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.textEnEsv: And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.textEnNkjv: And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took these and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.textEnNlt: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.textEnNasb: Nebuzaradan the captain of the bodyguards took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.textEn: Nebuzaradan the commander took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.textZh: 巴比伦王击打他们，在哈马地的利比拉把他们处死。这样，犹大人被掳，离开了他们的国土。
verses.textZhCnvs: 巴比伦王击打他们，在哈马地的利比拉把他们处死。这样，犹大人被掳，离开了他们的国土。
verses.textZhCuv: 巴比伦王就把他们击杀在哈马地的利比拉。这样，犹大人被掳去离开本地。
verses.textEnNiv: There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king had them executed. So Judah went into captivity, away from her land.
verses.textEnEsv: And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken into exile out of its land.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive from its own land.
verses.textEnNlt: And there at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon had them all put to death. So the people of Judah were sent into exile from their land.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was led into exile from its land.
verses.textEn: There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king had them executed. So Judah went into captivity, away from her land.

verses.textZh: 以下是尼布甲尼撒掳去的人民的数目：在他执政第七年，有犹大人三千零二十三名；
verses.textZhCnvs: 以下是尼布甲尼撒掳去的人民的数目：在他执政第七年，有犹大人三千零二十三名；
verses.textZhCuv: 尼布甲尼撒所掳的民数记在下面：在他第七年掳去犹大人三千零二十三名；
verses.textEnNiv: This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;
verses.textEnEsv: This is the number of the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year, 3,023 Judeans;
verses.textEnNkjv: These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Jews;
verses.textEnNlt: The number of captives taken to Babylon in the seventh year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign was 3,023.
verses.textEnNasb: These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar took into exile: in the seventh year 3,023 Jews;
verses.textEn: This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;

verses.textZh: 尼布甲尼撒第十八年，从耶路撒冷掳去的，有八百三十二人；
verses.textZhCnvs: 尼布甲尼撒第十八年，从耶路撒冷掳去的，有八百三十二人；
verses.textZhCuv: 尼布甲尼撒十八年从耶路撒冷掳去八百三十二人；
verses.textEnNiv: in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;
verses.textEnEsv: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem 832 persons;
verses.textEnNkjv: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred and thirty-two persons;
verses.textEnNlt: Then in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year he took 832 more.
verses.textEnNasb: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar 832 persons from Jerusalem;
verses.textEn: in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;

verses.textZh: 尼布甲尼撒第二十三年，护卫长尼布撒拉旦掳去犹大人七百四十五名。总数是四千六百人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 尼布甲尼撒第二十三年，护卫长尼布撒拉旦掳去犹大人七百四十五名。总数是四千六百人。
verses.textZhCuv: 尼布甲尼撒二十三年，护卫长尼布撒拉旦掳去犹大人七百四十五名；共有四千六百人。
verses.textEnNiv: in his twenty-third year, 745 Jews taken into exile by Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard. There were 4,600 people in all.
verses.textEnEsv: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Judeans 745 persons; all the persons were 4,600.
verses.textEnNkjv: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred and forty-five persons. All the persons were four thousand six hundred.
verses.textEnNlt: In Nebuchadnezzar’s twenty-third year he sent Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, who took 745 more—a total of 4,600 captives in all.
verses.textEnNasb: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took into exile 745 Jewish people; there were 4,600 people in all.
verses.textEn: in his twenty-third year, 745 Jews taken into exile by Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard. There were 4,600 people in all.

verses.textZh: 犹大王约雅斤被掳后第三十七年，就是巴比伦王以未．米罗达登基的那一年，十二月二十五日，他恩待 犹大王约雅斤，把他从狱中领出来，
verses.textZhCnvs: 犹大王约雅斤被掳后第三十七年，就是巴比伦王以未．米罗达登基的那一年，十二月二十五日，他恩待 犹大王约雅斤，把他从狱中领出来，
verses.textZhCuv: 犹大王约雅斤被掳后三十七年，巴比伦王以未‧米罗达元年十二月二十五日，使犹大王约雅斤抬头，提他出监，
verses.textEnNiv: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the year Awel-Marduk became king of Babylon, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he released Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison.
verses.textEnEsv: And in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, graciously freed Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
verses.textEnNlt: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of King Jehoiachin of Judah, Evil-merodach ascended to the Babylonian throne. He was kind to Jehoiachin and released him from prison on March 31 of that year.
verses.textEnNasb: Now it came about in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
verses.textEn: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the year Awel-Marduk became king of Babylon, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he released Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison.

verses.textZh: 并且安慰他，使他的地位高过和他一起在巴比伦的众王。
verses.textZhCnvs: 并且安慰他，使他的地位高过和他一起在巴比伦的众王。
verses.textZhCuv: 又对他说恩言，使他的位高过与他一同在巴比伦众王的位，
verses.textEnNiv: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.textEnEsv: And he spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.textEnNkjv: And he spoke kindly to him and gave him a more prominent seat than those of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.textEnNlt: He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and gave him a higher place than all the other exiled kings in Babylon.
verses.textEnNasb: Then he spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.textEn: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

verses.textZh: 又换下他的囚衣，赐他终生常在王面前吃饭。
verses.textZhCnvs: 又换下他的囚衣，赐他终生常在王面前吃饭。
verses.textZhCuv: 给他脱了囚服。他终身在巴比伦王面前吃饭。
verses.textEnNiv: So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king’s table.
verses.textEnEsv: So Jehoiachin put off his prison garments. And every day of his life he dined regularly at the king’s table,
verses.textEnNkjv: So Jehoiachin changed from his prison garments, and he ate bread regularly before the king all the days of his life.
verses.textEnNlt: He supplied Jehoiachin with new clothes to replace his prison garb and allowed him to dine in the king’s presence for the rest of his life.
verses.textEnNasb: So Jehoiachin changed his prison clothes, and had his meals in the king’s presence regularly all the days of his life.
verses.textEn: So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king’s table.

verses.textZh: 他的生活费用，在他一生的年日中，每日不断由巴比伦王供应，直到他去世的日子。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他的生活费用，在他一生的年日中，每日不断由巴比伦王供应，直到他去世的日子。
verses.textZhCuv: 巴比伦王赐他所需用的食物，日日赐他一分，终身是这样，直到他死的日子。
verses.textEnNiv: Day by day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived, till the day of his death.
verses.textEnEsv: and for his allowance, a regular allowance was given him by the king, according to his daily needs, until the day of his death, as long as he lived.
verses.textEnNkjv: And as for his provisions, there was a regular ration given him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
verses.textEnNlt: So the Babylonian king gave him a regular food allowance as long as he lived. This continued until the day of his death.
verses.textEnNasb: And as his allowance, a regular allowance was given to him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day, all the days of his life until the day of his death.
verses.textEn: Day by day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived, till the day of his death.
